title: Bench — where the framework is weakest now

panels.title: Weakest queries — recent vs all-time
panels.description: All-time and windowed pass rate per query, sorted by the regression, worst first. The window is the last N eligible sweeps set by the window_sweeps variable, not the time picker. Sweeps that are incomplete, filename-flagged INVALID, or re-costed duplicates of another sweep are excluded from both columns — admitting the INVALID sweep would drop 9 of the 10 public queries by 12.7 to 14.3 points, make the seven that truly sit at 100% read 85.7%, and evict both ASTPP sweeps from the window, inflating one ASTPP query by 16.7 points. Window sizes are thin: at the default of 8 the window holds 6 public and 2 ASTPP sweeps, so a public query has 18 runs and an ASTPP query 6, and one flipped run moves a public query 5.6 points and an ASTPP query 16.7. At a small window a whole query family can leave the table rather than read as a wrong number: at window 4 the four most recent eligible sweeps are all public-family, so all six ASTPP queries have no windowed runs and the table returns 10 rows instead of 16. Read the n columns before the percentages.

targets.rawSql:
WITH eligible AS (
    SELECT sweep_name, captured_at
    FROM bench.sweeps
    WHERE is_complete AND NOT is_flagged_invalid AND derived_from IS NULL
),
windowed AS (
    SELECT sweep_name FROM eligible
    ORDER BY captured_at DESC
    LIMIT (${window_sweeps:sqlstring})::int
),
win AS (
    SELECT r.query_id,
           count(*) AS n_recent,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.test_status = 'passed') AS p_recent
    FROM bench.runs r
    LEFT JOIN windowed w ON w.sweep_name = r.sweep_name
    WHERE w.sweep_name IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY r.query_id
),
hist AS (
    SELECT r.query_id,
           count(*) AS n_all,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.test_status = 'passed') AS p_all
    FROM bench.runs r
    LEFT JOIN eligible e ON e.sweep_name = r.sweep_name
    WHERE e.sweep_name IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY r.query_id
)
SELECT win.query_id                                            AS "query",
       round(100.0 * win.p_recent / win.n_recent, 1)           AS "recent %",
       win.n_recent                                            AS "recent n",
       round(100.0 * hist.p_all / hist.n_all, 1)               AS "all-time %",
       hist.n_all                                              AS "all-time n",
       round(100.0 * win.p_recent / win.n_recent
             - 100.0 * hist.p_all / hist.n_all, 1)             AS "delta pp"
FROM win
LEFT JOIN hist ON hist.query_id = win.query_id
ORDER BY "delta pp" ASC

panels.title: Flake by query
panels.description: All-time share of sweeps in which a query's repeats disagree with each other — one run passed, another failed, same code. Ranked per query on purpose: the aggregate across eligible sweeps is 16.0%, 97 split groups out of 608, which hides that the instability is concentrated in a handful of queries while the rest are solid. Groups with a single run are excluded, because one run cannot disagree with itself. Not moved by the time picker.

targets.rawSql:
WITH eligible AS (
    SELECT sweep_name FROM bench.sweeps
    WHERE is_complete AND NOT is_flagged_invalid AND derived_from IS NULL
),
groups AS (
    SELECT r.query_id, r.sweep_name,
           count(*) AS repeats,
           count(DISTINCT (r.test_status = 'passed')) AS distinct_outcomes
    FROM bench.runs r
    LEFT JOIN eligible e ON e.sweep_name = r.sweep_name
    WHERE e.sweep_name IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY r.query_id, r.sweep_name
    HAVING count(*) > 1
)
SELECT query_id                                              AS "query",
       count(*)                                              AS "sweeps",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE distinct_outcomes > 1)         AS "split sweeps",
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE distinct_outcomes > 1)
             / count(*), 1)                                  AS "flake %"
FROM groups
GROUP BY query_id
ORDER BY "flake %" DESC

panels.title: Failure shape per query
panels.description: All-time failure shape per query. The dryrun column reads the normalised value, not the raw CSV cell: a blank cell means the gate PASSED, because the pipeline reports the status only when it did not. 1,982 of 1,984 raw cells are blank, so treating blank as unknown would invert the main quality gate on almost the whole corpus. The gate-not-reached column is the separate case of a run that failed generation and never reached the gate at all: 5 such rows are visible here. The corpus holds 34, but 27 of them sit in the filename-flagged INVALID sweep and 2 in incomplete sweeps, both of which this panel excludes. step_budget_exhausted is populated on 52.1% of the rows this panel counts. Not moved by the time picker.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT r.query_id                                                        AS "query",
       count(*)                                                          AS "runs",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.generation_status = 'error')             AS "generation errors",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.test_status = 'failed')                  AS "test failures",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.dryrun_status_normalised = 'failed')     AS "dryrun failed",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.dryrun_status_normalised = 'not_reached') AS "gate not reached",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.step_budget_exhausted)                   AS "step budget exhausted"
FROM bench.runs r
LEFT JOIN bench.sweeps s ON s.sweep_name = r.sweep_name
WHERE s.is_complete AND NOT s.is_flagged_invalid AND s.derived_from IS NULL
GROUP BY r.query_id
ORDER BY "generation errors" DESC, "test failures" DESC

panels.title: Locator loss per query
panels.description: All-time per-element locator outcome, from the row-level total/successful/failed element counts, which are populated on 99.73% of the runs this panel counts — the 5 gaps are generation errors that never reached element identification, and they are skipped rather than read as zero. Deliberately NOT from element_approach_metrics: that array only ever records elements that WERE found, so a success rate computed from it is definitionally 100% and cannot express a failure. A per-approach breakdown stays unavailable until the browser service stops discarding the failure payload. Not moved by the time picker.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT r.query_id                                          AS "query",
       count(*)                                            AS "runs",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.failed_elements > 0)       AS "runs losing an element",
       sum(r.total_elements)                               AS "elements attempted",
       sum(r.successful_elements)                          AS "found",
       sum(r.failed_elements)                               AS "failed",
       round(100.0 * sum(r.successful_elements)
             / nullif(sum(r.total_elements), 0), 2)        AS "success %"
FROM bench.runs r
LEFT JOIN bench.sweeps s ON s.sweep_name = r.sweep_name
WHERE s.is_complete AND NOT s.is_flagged_invalid AND s.derived_from IS NULL
GROUP BY r.query_id
ORDER BY "success %" ASC NULLS LAST
